body.x: Human Performance Lab Co., Ltd., (CEO Taeyong Lee) participated in the 'Startup Zone' at the Eureka Park K-STARTUP integrated hall of 'CES 2023' in Las Vegas, USA from January 5 (Thursday) to 8 (Sunday, local time) for a total of 4 days.

Human Performance Lab is a company created in the biomechanics laboratory of Ewha Womans University, led by CEO Taeyong Lee, an expert in biomechanics. Under the vision of ‘Anytime, anywhere, anyone, every day is comfortable’, we research and develop contact-free customized insoles based on computer vision technology and computing simulation technology using numerical analysis. Through this, the difficulty of people with foot or lower limb pain having to visit the hospital or the store is being solved.

They were selected for the prospective startup package conducted by the Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development (KISED) and developed the MVP version of the customized insole production application ‘FitSole’ and was selected as the best company in the final inspection and was honored with a reward.

Human Performance Lab’s ‘FitSole’, which is based on 3D conversion algorithms and computer simulations, is a contact-free customized insole manufacturing system. The company explains that “perfectly customized insoles” and “contact-free foot measurement” are the key functions. FitSole produces customized insoles through filming a video of the foot surface only (around 10 seconds). Additionally, it uses FEM (Finite Element Method) walking simulation to choose the optimal shape and material. Accordingly, Human Performance Lab pointed out that it has the advantage of reducing 70% of the time it takes to measure the foot through FitSole, and that customized insoles can be provided to customers at a reasonable price by reducing labor costs.

A Human Performance Lab representative explained, “The insole is a part of the shoe that directly comes into contact with the sole (bottom of the foot) and plays a role in cushioning and shock absorption, greatly affecting the wearer’s gait and the comfort of the shoe. A generic insole that does not consider individual physical characteristics can lead to incorrect walking and increase the risk of foot and ankle diseases such as plantar fasciitis and intoe(hallux valgus), as well as various chronic diseases such as disc herniation and spinal diseases.”

He added, “Customized insoles that are tailored to the different shapes of people’s soles have an effect on gait correction and foot and heel pain relief and are particularly effective for people who experience persistent pain. Customized insoles are becoming more popular, but they are time-consuming and expensive to manufacture. Our company recognized this and developed the app ‘FitSole’, which allows users to order customized insoles through their smartphones and have them delivered to their doorstep.

He also told the background of their participation in the exhibition. A company official said, “We wanted to participate in CES 2023 to understand the current status of the healthcare market that is currently attracting attention. In addition, we aim to form a global partnership with Philips, and we would like to hold technical meetings with ‘Orthosensor’, a company that has the technology to periodically check and diagnose patients with feet and leg diseases in our target group. We are planning to develop slippers that reflect the curves of our feet in the future. In addition, we will further challenge the sports market, such as golf shoes and tennis shoes, using the data and technology we have accumulated.”

‘CES’ is the world’s biggest IT trade show and is a place where one can see the direction and trends of the appliance industry of the entire world. Hosted by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), it is held annually in Las Vegas, USA in January. Having reported on CES for 17 consecutive years, AVING News started reporting news of CES to the entire world since 2006, and conducted ‘BEST OF CES’, which chose the most innovative product and technology, and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA, which chose the best innovative company in Korea. In addition, it vividly relayed on-site issues in CES through ‘AVING LIVE’.

The K-STARTUP Joint Pavilion featured joint participation of institutions like the Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development, Seoul Business Agency, and Seoul Digital Foundation, as well as 51 Korean innovative companies, to enter the US market and discover global partners. In addition, university student supporters of CES 2023 chosen by each university (Kyunghee, Kookmin, Sogang, Chung-Ang) matched to participating companies based on their respective majors and fields of business.
